system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Seoul, South Korea. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Seoul itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Seoul space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Samcheong/Bukchon, Seochon/Tongui, Hannam/Itaewon, Cheongdam/Apgujeong, Euljiro/Jung-gu, Seongsu, Yeonhui/Mapo) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Seoul spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Seoul, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Kukje Gallery
galleries.note: Korea's most internationally connected gallery since 1982; represents Lee Ufan, Haegue Yang, Anish Kapoor and blue-chip Western estates, with a heavy Frieze/Art Basel presence.

galleries.name: Gallery Hyundai
galleries.note: Founded 1970, the oldest contemporary gallery in Korea; steward of Park Soo-keun, Kim Whanki, Nam June Paik and Lee Kun-Yong legacies alongside a strong younger programme.

galleries.name: PKM Gallery
galleries.note: Rigorous programme built around Yun Hyong-keun, Suh Se Ok, Olafur Eliasson and Cody Choi; a key driver of Dansaekhwa-era reappraisal abroad.

galleries.name: Hakgojae Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1988 a bridge between Korean modernism, minjung art and contemporary practice; strong scholarly exhibitions and international fair presence.

galleries.name: Arario Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Collector-founded gallery with a pan-Asian roster (Korea, China, India, Southeast Asia) and an appetite for difficult, research-driven work.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: First mega-gallery to commit to Seoul (2017, expanded 2021); anchors the Hannam gallery cluster with Yoshitomo Nara, Lee Kun-Yong and Pace's global roster.

galleries.name: Thaddaeus Ropac Seoul
galleries.note: Opened 2021 with museum-scale shows of Baselitz, Rauschenberg and Han Bing; central to Seoul's post-Frieze internationalisation.

galleries.name: Lehmann Maupin Seoul
galleries.note: In Seoul since 2017 in a SO-IL-designed space; long-running commitment to Do Ho Suh, Lee Bul, Sung Neung Kyung and Kim Yun Shin.

galleries.name: Perrotin Seoul
galleries.note: Early international arrival (2016) plus a Dosan Park space; blends global names with Korean artists such as Park Seo-Bo's late estate context and Bae Hyung-Kyung.

galleries.name: Gana Art
galleries.note: Founded 1983; large Pyeongchang-dong complex plus Hannam and Nine One spaces, historically decisive for Korean modern and minjung art markets.

galleries.name: Gladstone Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Opened 2021, bringing Anicka Yi, Alex Katz and Ugo Rondinone shows to Gangnam and legitimising Cheongdam as an international gallery district.

galleries.name: One and J. Gallery
galleries.note: The leading gallery of Korea's mid-career generation — Park Kyung-ryul, Jung Heeseung, Kang Seung Lee, Haneyl Choi — with consistent international fair placement.

galleries.name: Gallery Baton
galleries.note: Sharp, design-literate programme mixing Korean artists with European names; a fixture at Frieze, Art Basel and Liste.

galleries.name: Art Sonje Center
galleries.note: Seoul's most influential noncommercial kunsthalle since 1998; launched careers of Korean artists later shown at Venice and Documenta.

galleries.name: Barakat Contemporary
galleries.note: Contemporary arm of the antiquities dealer; ambitious curated shows of international mid-career artists and strong institutional collaborations.

galleries.name: Esther Schipper Seoul
galleries.note: Berlin gallery's Seoul outpost brings conceptual and installation-led practices (Philippe Parreno, Ryan Gander, Ann Veronica Janssens) to Korean audiences.

galleries.name: Various Small Fires (VSF) Seoul
galleries.note: LA gallery whose 2019 Seoul space was an early bet on the city; strong diasporic Korean-American and emerging international programme.

galleries.name: Peres Projects Seoul
galleries.note: Berlin gallery's Asian base since 2022, showing market-forward painting and a young international roster to Seoul collectors.

galleries.name: SongEun
galleries.note: Foundation space in a Herzog & de Meuron building; its SongEun Art Award has been a career-making platform for emerging Korean artists since 2001.

galleries.name: Whitestone Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Tokyo gallery's Kengo Kuma-designed Seoul space; Gutai and postwar Japanese material alongside contemporary Asian painting.

galleries.name: Tang Contemporary Art Seoul
galleries.note: Beijing/Hong Kong gallery's Seoul branch, one of the few venues consistently showing major Chinese contemporary artists in Korea.

galleries.name: Johyun Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Busan's leading gallery (Lee Bae, Kim Chong Hak) with a permanent Seoul space and a strong Frieze Seoul and international fair record.

galleries.name: Atelier Hermès
galleries.note: Corporate-funded, curator-led space whose Hermès Foundation Missulsang has been one of Korea's most prestigious art prizes.

galleries.name: Doosan Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Doosan Art Center's gallery and its residency/award pipeline in Seoul and New York are a key incubator for artists under 40.

galleries.name: P21
galleries.note: Lean, curatorially serious gallery with Korean and international emerging artists; regular at Liste and Frieze Seoul.

galleries.name: Gallery2
galleries.note: Long-running gallery with Palpan-dong and Pyeongchang-dong spaces, known for backing experimental Korean painters early.

galleries.name: Jason Haam
galleries.note: Young dealer with outsized international profile, showing Urs Fischer, Sarah Lucas and Ella Kruglyanskaya in Seoul.

galleries.name: PIBI Gallery
galleries.note: Quietly influential Samcheong gallery pairing established Korean conceptualists with strong younger sculptors and painters.

galleries.name: Chapter II
galleries.note: Early mover in Seongsu; contemporary programme of Korean and international emerging artists across multiple spaces.

galleries.name: Whistle
galleries.note: Critically respected small gallery representing young Korean artists with a conceptual, materially inventive bent.

galleries.name: BB&M
galleries.note: Founded 2021 by veteran dealers; museum-quality shows of Korean artists including Kim Beom-adjacent conceptual practices.

galleries.name: Alternative Space Loop
galleries.note: Korea's first alternative space (1999), a foundational platform for media, performance and Asian curatorial exchange.

galleries.name: Leeahn Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: Daegu-founded gallery with a permanent Seoul space; solid Korean modern-contemporary crossovers and international fair activity.

galleries.name: Space Willing N Dealing
galleries.note: Hybrid gallery/project space known for rigorous curatorial framing of emerging Korean artists and criticism-led programming.

galleries.name: Gallery Simon
galleries.note: Seochon mainstay showing Korean conceptual and media artists; a steady presence at domestic fairs since the 1990s.

galleries.name: Gallery Chosun
galleries.note: Long-running Samcheong gallery with an experimental, artist-friendly programme and open-call exhibitions.

galleries.name: Foundry Seoul
galleries.note: Well-funded exhibition space opened 2022 with ambitious curated group shows of international contemporary art.

galleries.name: Amado Art Space
galleries.note: Nonprofit with influential awards for artists and art critics, supporting research-based practice outside the market.

galleries.name: Gallery Shilla Seoul
galleries.note: Daegu gallery (est. 1992) with a Seoul space; Korean postwar experimental art and international minimal/conceptual figures.

galleries.name: 313 Art Project
galleries.note: Design-inflected Cheongdam gallery bringing European contemporary artists to Korean collectors.

galleries.name: Park Ryu Sook Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1983; pioneering in introducing international contemporary artists to Seoul and supporting Korean sculptors.

galleries.name: Gallery Bhak
galleries.note: Veteran gallery (est. 1983) with a strong Korean modern and abstract painting programme.

galleries.name: Sun Gallery
galleries.note: Insadong institution since 1977; historically important for Korean modern painting and Sun Contemporary's younger arm.

galleries.name: Kwanhoon Gallery
galleries.note: One of Insadong's oldest galleries, a barometer of the traditional Korean art trade with regular contemporary shows.

galleries.name: Ihn Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established Samcheong gallery with a quiet, connoisseurial programme of Korean modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Gallery Skape
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery known for design-conscious installations and emerging Korean artists since the mid-2000s.

galleries.name: ThisWeekendRoom
galleries.note: Youth-oriented gallery that helped launch a generation of Korean painters now on the international fair circuit.

galleries.name: Cylinder
galleries.note: Fast-rising young gallery with two Seoul spaces; a bellwether for the post-2020 emerging Korean scene.

galleries.name: N/A
galleries.note: Small, critically attentive gallery for emerging Korean and international artists, active at young-gallery fairs.

galleries.name: Hall1
galleries.note: Architecturally striking Hannam space with a tightly curated contemporary programme.

galleries.name: Gallery Kiche
galleries.note: Focused programme of Korean and Japanese contemporary artists with careful, restrained installations.

galleries.name: Choi&Choi Gallery
galleries.note: Cologne-Seoul gallery introducing European emerging artists to Korea and Korean artists to Germany.

galleries.name: Keumsan Gallery
galleries.note: Long-standing gallery with Korea-Japan exchange exhibitions and a Heyri satellite.

galleries.name: Trunk Gallery
galleries.note: Photography-focused gallery that has been central to the market for contemporary Korean photography.

galleries.name: Gallery Lux
galleries.note: Dedicated photography gallery supporting emerging photographers through consistent solo exhibitions.

galleries.name: Space K Seoul
galleries.note: Kolon-funded nonprofit in a Mass Studies-designed building; free, well-produced solo shows by Korean and international artists.

galleries.name: Ilwoo Space
galleries.note: Foundation space whose Ilwoo Photography Award is one of the most significant prizes for Korean photographers.

galleries.name: Arko Art Center
galleries.note: Arts Council Korea's public gallery in a Kim Swoo-geun building; long-running platform for mid-career Korean artists.

galleries.name: Art Space Pool
galleries.note: Historic alternative space and publisher with a politically engaged, discourse-driven programme since 1999.

galleries.name: d/p
galleries.note: Euljiro project space combining exhibitions with critical writing and publishing on emerging practice.

galleries.name: Audio Visual Pavilion
galleries.note: Idiosyncratic artist-run space in a hanok alley, influential in Seoul's small-scale experimental scene.

galleries.name: Boan1942
galleries.note: Former inn turned cultural complex with galleries, residencies and publishing; a hub of Seochon's art community.

galleries.name: WESS
galleries.note: Curator-run space with research-heavy exhibitions and a reputation for spotting artists before institutions do.

galleries.name: Hapjungjigu
galleries.note: Artist-run Mapo space known for feminist and queer-inflected programming and emerging artists' first solos.

galleries.name: Post Territory Ujeongguk
galleries.note: Converted post office running interdisciplinary exhibitions, performance and discourse programmes.

galleries.name: Primary Practice
galleries.note: Small Euljiro space typical of the district's DIY scene, showing young artists and design-art crossovers.

galleries.name: PS Center
galleries.note: Independent space in central Seoul mixing exhibitions, performance and publishing for a younger audience.

galleries.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Seoul
galleries.note: Free exhibition space atop the Frank Gehry-designed Maison, presenting Fondation Louis Vuitton collection works.

galleries.name: Storage by Hyundai Card
galleries.note: Corporate-run underground exhibition hall commissioning large-scale installations by international artists.

galleries.name: The Page Gallery
galleries.note: Seongsu gallery with a strong Korean abstraction and international mid-career programme in a large industrial space.

galleries.name: Artside Gallery
galleries.note: Longtime Korea-China exchange gallery, one of the first to introduce Beijing avant-garde artists to Seoul.

galleries.name: Gallery ERD
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a design and craft-adjacent programme and consistent emerging-artist solos.

galleries.name: Gallery EM
galleries.note: Cheongdam gallery known for photography and media-based Korean artists.

galleries.name: Gallery Yeh
galleries.note: Established Gangnam gallery with a Korean modern and contemporary painting programme and deep collector base.

galleries.name: Opera Gallery Seoul
galleries.note: International secondary-market chain whose Seoul branch is a significant conduit for blue-chip modern works.

galleries.name: Jinsun Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running Jongno gallery with a steady programme of Korean painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: Gallery Grimson
galleries.note: Bukchon gallery supporting mid-career Korean artists with an accessible, consistent exhibition schedule.

galleries.name: Gallery Dam
galleries.note: Small hanok-area gallery with an intimate programme of drawing, painting and artist books.

galleries.name: Space So
galleries.note: Compact independent space in Seochon showing experimental work by early-career artists.

galleries.name: Weekend
galleries.note: Artist-organised space with short, focused exhibitions that feed Seoul's emerging-gallery pipeline.

galleries.name: Space22
galleries.note: Photography-dedicated nonprofit space in Gangnam supporting documentary and contemporary photographers.

galleries.name: Kunstdoc
galleries.note: Alternative space with international residency exchanges and experimental exhibition programming.

galleries.name: Gallery Joeun
galleries.note: Yongsan gallery showing Korean contemporary painting and sculpture with regular domestic fair participation.

galleries.name: Sun Contemporary
galleries.note: Contemporary arm of Sun Gallery, focused on younger Korean artists and media-based work.

galleries.name: Everyday Mooonday
galleries.note: Popular Seongsu gallery for young figurative painters and illustration-adjacent contemporary art, with a large collector following.
